$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — the `agents` canonical store. One
entry per scope filter, per refusal mapping, per lock, per ordering and per
null-handling decision, each carrying the file it lives in, the EXACT text
that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED
cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A FIFTH FILE BESIDE mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json AND mutations-outbox.json rather than an extension of
any of them, because the five tranches are five separate claims about five
separate port surfaces and a reader checking one should not have to read past
the other four. All five are hashed by the same packages.adapters.config rule
and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. Almost every guard here is a WHERE
clause or an error mapping, and both are invisible to an assertion on a happy
path: a scope filter that has been deleted returns MORE rows, which no test
that asks for the row it just wrote will ever notice, and a refusal mapping
that has been deleted turns a business outcome into a rejected promise, which
a test that only reads `result.ok` on the success path will never see. The
one guard that is not of that kind — the savepoint — changes no returned
value at all and can only be seen from a SECOND connection.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep
unless it is green with a non-zero test count, and classifies a run with no
executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
For one entry: replace its `from` with its `to` in the named file (the driver
requires the `from` to occur EXACTLY ONCE, so a stale entry is an error and
not a silent no-op), run the named suites against a real PostgreSQL container,
and confirm a NAMED case in `kills` is among the failures. Then revert and
confirm green again.
ALL BUT SEVEN NEED A REAL POSTGRESQL, and none of those could have been written
against a double. The seven that do not are M-A07, M-A08 and M-A30, M-A31 on

the two modules here with no database in them, `agents-guards.ts` and
`agents-rows.ts`.
TWO GUARDS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THIS LEDGER, and saying so is the
point of this paragraph rather than a footnote. `updateAgent` writes
`projectId` and `updateCluster` writes `environmentId` so that the
`reject_canonical_owner_change` rules can refuse a moved record; removing
either column from the write does not make a test fail, it makes the write
SUCCEED where it used to be refused — which is a change in behaviour a
mutation of the guard cannot express, because the guard IS the extra column.
The refusal each one produces is pinned instead, in
`agents-constraints.integration.test.ts`, from the store's own answer.

result: THIRTY-ONE ENTRIES, THIRTY-ONE KILLS, NONE VACUOUS AND NONE SURVIVING, on a
real PostgreSQL container. Each kill is a NAMED case in the `kills` list of
its entry. The driver proved all EIGHT distinct suite sets green before it
mutated anything -- 21, 12, 18, 16, 14, 2, 11 and 7 executed cases -- and
classified nothing as vacuous. Those eight figures reconcile against the
census: transaction 12 + statements 9, transaction 12, constraints 16 +
conformance 2, constraints 16, guards 14, conformance 2, conformance 2 +
statements 9, rows 7.
RE-RUN END TO END AFTER THE WAVE WAS STOPPED AND REVIVED, because the sweep
above had been recorded and never verified on this branch: the tranche was
killed mid-flight and its last commit is a salvage the builder did not make.
The second run is the one this file now reports -- 31/31 killed, 0 survived,
0 vacuous, 0 stale, 0 build-failed, against pgvector/pgvector:pg16 -- and it
agrees with the first entry for entry.
SWEPT A THIRD TIME, BY A DRIVER WRITTEN FROM THIS FILE RATHER THAN WITH IT,
after the wave was stopped a second time. The paragraphs above were recorded
by the builder that produced the entries, and a ledger checked only by the
hand that wrote it is a claim rather than evidence. The third run reads the
`from`/`to`/`suites`/`kills` of each entry, requires the `from` to occur
EXACTLY ONCE, proves each distinct suite set green before mutating anything,
and reads vitest's executed-case count out of the `Tests` summary line in
BOTH shapes it prints -- `N passed (N)` and `N failed | M passed (T)` -- so a
run in which every case dies is a kill and not vacuity.
It agrees with this file entry for entry: the same eight baselines, green in
the same order -- 21, 12, 18, 16, 14, 2, 11, 7 -- then 31 entries, 31 KILLED,
0 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS, 0 STALE, each by a NAMED case from its own `kills`
list, against pgvector/pgvector:pg16 on the same machine the integration
suites run on. The working tree was byte-identical afterwards.
THE DRIVER DOES NOT REBUILD BETWEEN MUTATIONS, and that is a departure from
the earlier tranches' drivers worth naming rather than hiding. Every entry
here mutates a file under `src/`, and every suite that reads one imports it
RELATIVELY -- vitest transforms the .ts and dist is never consulted. The only
dist this package needs is the CONTEXTS it imports across the workspace, and
no entry touches one. Checked before the sweep rather than assumed: M-A07 was
swept alone with the rebuild removed, its unmutated baseline was green, and it
died on its named case.
THREE OF THE THIRTY-ONE DID NOT DIE ON THE FIRST SWEEP, and the three are the
part of this file worth reading, because each one was a guard that nothing
could turn red:
M-A07 and M-A08 read a refusal out of `meta` rather than out of the message
text, which is the shape a RAW statement's refusal arrives in. Both
SURVIVED: every refusable write in this adapter is a DELEGATE call, so the
raw shape is real, observed, handled -- and unreached. They are falsified
now in `agents-guards.test.ts`, against the exact error objects copied off
a container, rather than deleted as dead code.
M-A13 asks whether `countBindings` resolves its client through
`writer(scope)` or through `reader()`. It SURVIVED, and the reason is worth
stating: `reader()` PREFERS the open ambient transaction, so the count is
correct either way. What `writer(scope)` adds is the three transaction-scope
refusals, so the guard is not the count at all -- it is that a token from a
transaction which has already finished is REFUSED. The case that kills it
now asserts exactly that.
ONE MORE ENTRY WAS MIS-CLASSIFIED RATHER THAN WRONG, and the driver was fixed
instead of the entry. M-A29 -- the nullable-JSONB null -- was reported VACUOUS
on the first sweep. It had in fact killed both conformance cases; the driver
counted executed cases with a pattern that required `N passed` on vitest's
summary line, and a run in which every case fails prints no such group. A
driver that reports a kill as vacuity is the same defect as one that reports
vacuity as a kill.
NOTHING SURVIVED IN THE END, AND THAT IS WORTH ONE SENTENCE OF SUSPICION
rather than a victory lap. The entries that would have survived a weaker
suite are the ones to look at. M-A01 removes the SAVEPOINT and changes NO
returned value -- only a read from a SECOND connection can see it. M-A16 and
M-A17 remove the row lock and its LEFT JOIN, and change no value either: only
an assertion on the ORDER of events across two concurrent transactions sees
the first, and only a concurrent pair over an agent with NO VERSIONS AT ALL
sees the second. M-A13 changes nothing observable except a refusal. Every one
of those cases exists because the first draft of this tranche did not have it.
